data.cultural_impact: The name "Rohtash" is of Sanskrit origin, derived from the Sanskrit words "Rohana," meaning chariot, and "Thash," meaning God. In Hindu culture, the deity Vishnu is often depicted riding a chariot drawn by celestial horses to protect and provide for his devotees. The name Rohtash signifies someone who is not just protected by God, but also believed to be blessed and favored by the divine, thus carrying a deep sense of pride and reverence in society.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Rohtash" also holds great spiritual significance as it highlights the belief in divine protection. According to Hinduism, every soul is an expression of God, and Rohtash is a reminder that the Gods are always present and offering their protection to their devotees. It encourages devotion, faith, and the pursuit of a virtuous path in life, as it is believed that the Gods shower their blessings upon those who lead righteous lives.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Rohtash in Hinduism symbolizes the radiant and righteous one. The celestial body, Rohini star, is also associated with this name, reflecting inner light and moral guidance.

historical_references.reference: Rohtash is believed to be an ancient name for the city of Rohtak in Haryana, India. It is mentioned in the Mahabharata, an epic Sanskrit text that forms a part of the Indian subcontinent's Hindu scriptures. The name Rohtash is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Rohana' and 'Tashta', which mean 'Horse' and 'Exalted One' respectively.

Another reference to Rohtash can be found in the 12th-century Sanskrit text 'Bhagavat Purana'. In this text, Rohtas is mentioned as a king who ruled over the region of Rohet in Rajasthan. He is described as a pious and benevolent king who ruled his kingdom with justice.

modern_usage.modern_context: Rohtash is a modern character seen in Indian comic books published by Marvel, as well as in the animated TV series Chhota Bheem. In Chhota Bheem, Rohtash is a friend of the main character, helping him solve various challenges and adventures. Overall, Rohtash is becoming a popular character in various modern contexts, including comic books and animation, reflecting the enduring influence of Hindu mythology in Indian culture.
